V1.scale: REVISED MECHANISM: Measurements show Java heap is constant (~11 MB allocated, ~11 MB peak heap) regardless of decompressed output size (2–64 MB). BrotliDecoder.pull() calls alloc.buffer(int), and the default PooledByteBufAllocator creates direct (off-heap) ByteBufs. The growing resource is direct memory, not Java heap. Direct memory grows at ~1 byte per byte of decompressed output (inferred: all output ByteBufs accumulate unreleased in the out list during a single decode() call). Wall time grows at ~1.29 ms/MB (measured over 4–64 MB). To exhaust MaxDirectMemorySize (which defaults to Xmx = 1 GB): ~1 GB of decompressed output is needed, taking ~1.4 seconds (well under the 20-second timeout). Brotli compresses 1 GB of zeros to ~1642 bytes; all-zeros is near-optimal for brotli compression, so no significantly denser encoding exists.

V2.scale: REVISED: Measurements show allocated grows at ~1.04 MB per MB of decompressed output (linear from 16–64 MB), but peak heap plateaus at ~38 MB for 32–64 MB of decompressed data. ZstdDecoder.decode() explicitly uses ctx.alloc().heapBuffer(), so data is heap-allocated, but the PooledByteBufAllocator's arena management keeps peak live heap far below cumulative allocations. Wall time grows at ~1.72 ms/MB. Extrapolating to 256 MB decompressed (maximum from a 10240-byte zstd input of ~8210 bytes compressed): ~280 MB allocated, peak heap likely ~50–80 MB, ~549 ms wall time. With -Xmx1g, neither OOM (280 MB allocated << 1 GB) nor timeout (549 ms << 20 s) is triggered. For OOM at ~900 MB allocated: ~851 MB decompressed is needed, requiring ~27449 bytes of compressed zstd, which exceeds the 10240-byte input limit. The failure cannot occur within this evaluation's input size limit.
